candidate_relations.reason: Miller Fisher is a different cranial neuropathy syndrome and does not explain post-traumatic orthostatic headache with recumbency-improving diplopia.
Superior orbital fissure syndrome is a different anatomic localization and does not capture cerebrospinal fluid hypovolemia.
The motor-vehicle crash is a plausible precipitant of CSF leak but traumatic brain injury is not the requested hypovolemia diagnosis.
Orbital myositis is a different inflammatory orbital disease and does not account for orthostatic headache after trauma.
Left ptosis and diplopia can reflect cranial-nerve dysfunction from CSF hypovolemia, but third-nerve palsy is a manifestation rather than the final object, and pupils and ductions are spared.
Post-traumatic cranial nerve palsy describes the ocular findings after the crash but omits the orthostatic CSF-hypovolemia mechanism.
Baroreflex failure is a different cause of orthostatic symptoms and does not produce recumbency-improving diplopia after trauma.
Brown syndrome is a restrictive trochlear disorder unrelated to cerebrospinal fluid hypovolemia.
Traumatic cranial nerve palsy is a related description of post-crash ocular findings, not the CSF hypovolemia syndrome.
Lambert-Eaton syndrome is a different neuromuscular diagnosis; AChR and edrophonium testing here targeted myasthenia, not LEMS, and orthostatic headache is unexplained.
Myasthenia gravis was the explicit ocular differential and was contradicted by negative AChR antibody and edrophonium tests; it is not CSF hypovolemia.
Kearns-Sayre is a different mitochondrial syndrome not supported by the examination or history.
Botulism is a different descending paralysis syndrome and does not fit isolated orthostatic ocular symptoms months after trauma.
Cranial nerve palsy names a manifestation of CSF hypovolemia without the required hypovolemia diagnosis.
Ocular myasthenia was considered and not supported by negative antibody and edrophonium testing; it is not the reference object.
Diphtheria is a different infectious neuropathy and is unrelated to this post-traumatic orthostatic presentation.
Superior oblique myokymia is a different ocular motility disorder and does not explain orthostatic headache.
Mitochondrial myopathy is a different systemic myopathic entity not indicated by the record.
Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome is a different metabolic encephalopathy and is not supported here.
CPEO is a different chronic ophthalmoplegia and does not produce acute orthostatic headache after trauma.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate; reference CSF hypovolemia is not named, and opening pressure/MRI confirmation is absent from the record.
